newsitem.title: QATAR: Most OPEC members want output ceiling held - Badri.
newsitem.headline: Most OPEC members want output ceiling held - Badri.

text.p: OPEC President Abdullah Salem al-Badri said on Saturday he believed most members in the group would favour sticking to their current production ceiling at their next ministerial meeting in June.
The Libyan oil minister said he had met most of his counterparts in the 11-member OPEC and "came to the conclusion that everybody wants a rollover of the ceiling," for the next six months.
He was speaking to reporters in Doha after talks with his Qatari counterpart, Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah. Both said they agreed the current production ceiling should be maintained.

Badri arrived earlier from the Iranian city Asfahan, where he and six other ministers in the group's committee charged with examining quota compliance met on the sidelines of a weekend energy conference.

The ministers, from Libya, Iran, Nigeria, Venezuela, Kuwait, Qatar and Indonesia agreed oil markets were oversupplied with crude, and they should act quickly to bolster prices for the rest of the year.

The committee decided that whoever was overproducing should return to quota, Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh said afterwards, adding all the ministers were seriously concerned about the state of the market.
Badri said he would travel this week to Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates to see what they had to say before the meeting in Vienna next month.
OPEC production is running above 27 million barrels a day (bpd), two million bpd above the group ceiling.
Badri said he was trying to underline to OPEC producers the need for discipline in order to shore up prices, which have sagged to around $18 a barrel this year.
"If everybody adheres to their quota, then the prices will go up", he said.
Attiyah said: "I hope OPEC will work hard to stabilise the market and protect prices. We must remember a drop in prices will negatively affect all producers -- OPEC and non-OPEC".
"Ceilings should be maintained to support prices," he added.
